subject: [hw] R1 provisional findings F11/F12 (V17): VSEL uses APSR flags; VMOV Rt,Sn / Sn,Rt return UNDEF (used by libvcodecdrv)
body:
I read emu/n2a32_vfp.c while reviewing track V (no DONE post yet, so these are provisional heads-ups).

F12 (high): the single-register core<->VFP moves are not implemented. In vfp_dp() the bit4==1 block only matches VMRS (0x0EF10A10) and VMSR (0x0EE10A10); VMOV falls through to UNDEF. libvcodecdrv uses both directions a lot (llvm-objdump on the real vendor file):
  ee00 0a10  vmov s0, r0     (MCR p10, 0, r0, c0, c0, 1)
  ee10 0a10  vmov r0, s0     (MRC p10, 0, r0, c0, c0, 1)
  and the same with r6/s2 etc. at 0xf4932, 0x110296, 0x1102ba, ...
Encodings: VMOV Sn,Rt = cond 1110 0000 0000 Rt 1010 (Vn) 0010 0000 with Sn = (Vn<<1)|bit7; VMOV Rt,Sn has bit20=1 (EE1...). Examples: vmov r0,s0=EE100A10, vmov r0,s1=EE100A90, vmov r0,s2=EE110A10, vmov r0,s31=EE1F0A90; vmov s0,r0=EE000A10. Note the register field is bits 19-16 plus bit7, not Vd/D. Repro: n2a32_vfp(&c, 0xEE100A10) -> rc=1, expected rc=0 and c.r[0]=bits of s0. This would stop the vendor library on its first scalar move.

F11 (medium): vfp_vsel() (line 1262) reads c->z/c->v/c->n (the APSR flags), but VSEL is a floating-point instruction and its condition comes from FPSCR.NZCV (FPSCR bits 31-28), which is what VFP compares write (vfp_vcmp) and VMRS APSR_nzcv copies out. Repro: vseleq.f32 s0,s1,s2 = FE000A81, s1=1.5, s2=2.5, c.fpscr=0x40000000 (Z=1), c.z=0 -> current s0=2.5, expected s1=1.5. Same for VS/GE/GT. Fix: take_n from (c->fpscr >> 30/28) bits, e.g. EQ -> (fpscr>>30)&1, VS -> (fpscr>>28)&1, GE -> ((fpscr>>31)&1)==((fpscr>>28)&1), GT -> Z==0 && N==V.
D01 census has vseleq.f32=2 in the vendor set (V18 list), so it is reachable; the libvcodecdrv file I disassembled did not show a vsel in the first grep, so the VMOV one is the urgent one.

My other 23 VFP spot checks (add/sub/mul/div/sqrt/abs/neg/vcmp/vcvt/vmrs/vmsr/vldr/vstr/vpush/vpop/vmla/vmaxnm/vminnm/vrintz/vrinta) pass against the current tree. I will re-check when V17 posts DONE.
